Structural identification schemes

Source: R/id.R
identification.Rd

Each constructor returns a small specification object consumed by dynamics, and friends. The reduced-form innovations are \(u_t = P \varepsilon_t\), \(E[\varepsilon_t\varepsilon_t']=I\); an identification scheme picks \(P\) with \(PP' = \Sigma\).

Usage

id_chol(order = NULL)

id_longrun()

id_given(P)

id_sign(restrictions, horizon = 1L, nrot = 1L, maxtry = 1000L)

Arguments

order

<tidy-select> variable ordering (first = most exogenous), e.g. order = c(rate, infl, unemp); names, strings and positions all work. Defaults to the column order of the data.

P

a K x K impact matrix.

restrictions

a K x K matrix (rows: variables, columns: shocks) or a K x K x H array with entries +1, -1 (sign) or 0 (unrestricted). Dimnames are used to label the shocks. Columns of all zeros are unidentified shocks.

horizon

if restrictions is a matrix, the number of horizons (from impact) over which the restriction is imposed.

nrot

number of accepted rotations to keep per reduced-form draw.

maxtry

maximum rotations tried per reduced-form draw.

Details

  • id_chol() recursive (Cholesky) ordering, Sims (1980).

  • id_longrun() Blanchard-Quah (1989): the cumulative long-run effect matrix is lower triangular.

  • id_sign() sign restrictions on impulse responses (Uhlig 2005; Rubio-Ramirez, Waggoner & Zha 2010).

  • id_given() user supplied impact matrix \(P\).

See also

Other identification: id_hetero(), id_proxy(), id_restrictions(), id_zerosign(), irf_fry_pagan(), proxy_draws()

Examples

fit <- varm(yraw, p = 2)
id_chol(order = c(rate, infl, unemp))
#> <varm_id> recursive (Cholesky), order: c(rate, infl, unemp)
#> (first = most exogenous; the contemporaneous effect of later variables on earlier ones is zero)
irf(fit, id_chol(order = c(rate, infl, unemp)), horizon = 4, ci = "none")
#> <varm IRF> K = 3, horizon 0..4, id = chol

S <- matrix(c(1, 1, 1, 1, -1, 0, 1, 0, 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)
id_sign(S)
#> <varm_id> sign restrictions (6 at impact; 1 horizon)
#>   + positive, - negative, · unrestricted; rows = variables, cols = shocks
#>   rotations: 1 per draw, max 1000 tries
#>    e1 e2 e3
#> v1  +  +  +
#> v2  +  -  ·
#> v3  +  ·  ·
